title: SF2522 (2019-2020 Regular): Firearm transferee permit hearing modification

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Minnesota) (gun-policy Stage 5, Minnesota); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Minnesota text (Introduction; official copy, https://www.revisor.mn.gov/bills/91/2019/0/SF/2522/versions/0/)
provenance.note: Read the introduced bill (no date in file); no vote data. The text strikes the old one-sentence appeal rule. The quote keeps the printed typo 'tranferee'.

operative_text:
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 8(a)): Any person aggrieved by denial, revocation, or failure to timely issue a tranferee permit may appeal by petition to the district court with jurisdiction over the county or municipality where the application was submitted.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 8(b)): The district court must hold a hearing at the earliest practicable date and in any event no later than 14 days following the filing of the petition for review.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 8(c)): The court must issue its writ of mandamus directing that the permit be issued and order other appropriate relief unless the chief of police or sheriff establishes by clear and convincing evidence that the applicant is disqualified under the criteria described in subdivision 4.
Section 1 (Minn. Stat. 624.7131, subd. 8(d)): If the court grants a petition under paragraph (b), the court must award the applicant reasonable costs and expenses including attorney fees.
